question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}p+q=1 \\ -2p-3q=1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $5.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}p+q=1 & |\,\times 5 \\ -2p-3q=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2p+5q=5 \\ -2p-3q=1\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $2p$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-2p$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $p$-variable, and allows us to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{2p}+5q & =5 \\ -\cancel{2p}-3q & =1 \\ 2q & =6 \\ q & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $q=3$ into the equation $2p+5q=5$ to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2p+5q & =5 \\ 2p+5\cdot 3 & =5 \\ 2p+15 & =5 \\ 2p & =-10 \\ p & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $p=-5$ and $q=3.$
